review_notes: Read the whole file and checked its uses (BaseEulerSign, BaseEulerGuards, BaseEulerState, TransversePacketTimeData, etc.) and SmoothTimeField.derivativeField_eq. Findings are about how the simp set interacts, from reading the declarations. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim about exact simp behaviour or priorities. Rewriting of `inverse.field`/`frame.field` by the simp lemmas is by reading only. Other simp lemmas (first_apply, second_apply, curvature_apply) looked reasonable.

findings.declaration: EulerParentPacketFrames.Parent.inverse_apply (with frame_apply, strain_apply; versus inverse_left / inverse_right / inverse_initial)
findings.excerpt:
@[simp] theorem inverse_apply (t : Icc (0 : ℝ) G.T) (x : Space) :
    G.inverse.field t x = adjugate (G.frame.field t x) := rfl
findings.problem: The simp set unfolds the abstract `G.inverse.field t x` to `adjugate (G.frame.field t x)`, and `frame_apply` (also simp) then expands `G.frame.field t x` to `id + fderiv ℝ (G.displacement.field t) (G.ell • x)`. This expansion competes with the file's own algebraic interface. The statements `inverse_left`, `inverse_right`, `inverse_initial` and `strain_equation` have LHS patterns `G.inverse.field t x (G.frame.field t x v)`. Once the two simp lemmas fire first, those patterns no longer match, so they could not be tagged `@[simp]` and are not usable by simp. Downstream code accordingly never uses simp here. It does manual `rw [G.strain_apply, comp_apply, G.inverse_initial]` (BaseEulerSign, BaseEulerGuards). `inverse_apply` and `strain_apply` are also tagged simp even though their RHS (an adjugate of the full frame, or a `comp` of the unfolded pieces) is not a better normal form. The adjugate is only meaningful together with `frame_det`, which simp cannot supply.
findings.proposed_change: Drop `@[simp]` from `inverse_apply` (and probably `strain_apply`) and keep them as plain `rw` unfolding lemmas. Keep `frame_apply`, `first_apply` and `second_apply`, whose RHS is the intended canonical `fderiv` form. Then add `inverse_left`, `inverse_right` and `inverse_initial` as simp lemmas. Their LHS (`G.inverse.field t x (G.frame.field t x v)`) is then not preempted by `inverse_apply`/`frame_apply`, and neither of those lemmas needs priority tweaks. If `inverse_apply` stays simp, `inverse_left`/`inverse_right` should carry `(priority := high)` and be checked to fire before the unfolding.
findings.benefit: `simp` could then discharge `G.inverse.field t x (G.frame.field t x v) = v` and the `strain`/`second` rewrites directly. Downstream proofs would not need long chains of explicit `rw [G.strain_apply, comp_apply, G.inverse_initial, ...]`. Goals would also not blow up into `adjugate (id + fderiv ...)` terms that the determinant hypothesis cannot reduce.

findings.excerpt:
@[simp] theorem initialStrain_apply (x : Space) :
    G.initialStrain.field x = G.first.field G.zeroTime x := rfl
findings.problem: `frame_initial` (and `inverse_initial`) state the normal form at time `G.zeroTime`, but they are not simp lemmas. Any simp call sees `G.frame.field G.zeroTime x` and rewrites it with the existing simp lemma `frame_apply` into `id + fderiv ℝ (G.displacement.field G.zeroTime) (G.ell • x)`. Nothing then reduces that, because `initial` is stated for `⟨0,le_rfl,T_pos.le⟩`, not for `G.zeroTime`, and `zeroTime` is a def that simp does not unfold. Likewise `initialStrain_apply` yields `G.first.field G.zeroTime x`, which `first_apply` expands to `fderiv ℝ (G.velocity.field G.zeroTime) (G.ell • x)`, a form that has lost the connection to the initial strain. So the evaluation-at-zero API is left to manual `rw`. Callers use `change ...; rw [G.frame_initial, id_apply]` (BaseEulerSign) and `rw [Parent.initialStrain_apply, Parent.first_apply]` (BaseEulerState).
findings.proposed_change: Make `frame_initial` and `inverse_initial` `@[simp]`, with higher priority than `frame_apply` and `inverse_apply` (or restrict those to `t` not syntactically `zeroTime`). `inverse_initial` is stated with an explicit `v`, which suits simp. Optionally add a `@[simp]` lemma `zeroTime_val : (G.zeroTime : ℝ) = 0`. Keep the `@[simp] initialStrain_apply` only if `first_apply` unfolding at zero is the intended normal form. Otherwise state it in terms of the initial frame.
findings.benefit: Goals evaluated at `zeroTime` would simplify to the identity frame and inverse (and the strain to `first ∘ id`) in one `simp` call. Currently those cases need a hand-written `change`/`rw` sequence, and a bare `simp` can leave an opaque `fderiv` expression at zero time.
